power consumption in memory checker circuits can be reduced with little or no increase in area or delay by selecting the parity check matrices of the error correcting codes that are used to perform ECC.

the power consumed in single-error-correcting, double-error-detecting checker-circuits can be reduced by up to 27-41% with little or no increase in area and delay, by selecting the parity-check matrix of the error-correcting code.

power optimization of SEC-DED codes can be performed with a genetic algorithm or with simulated annealing, that both algorithms perform well, and that the power optimization can result in significant power savings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problem.
power optimization of memory ECC checker circuits.
the design of memory checker circuits that perform error correcting codes, and the minimization of power in these checker circuits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a non-linear optimization approach, in the form of genetic algorithms or simulated annealing, can result in significant power reductions in memory ECC checker circuits.
the power reduction achieved by using genetic algorithms is significantly higher than that achieved with simulated annealing.
the use of genetic algorithms for the optimization of power in memory checker circuits is recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach provides a practical and efficient method to reduce power consumption in single error correcting, double error detecting memory checker circuits.

power-aware code selection can result in significant power savings with minimal impact on area and timing, and that genetic algorithms can be used as a practical alternative to simulated annealing for this problem.
the power optimization problem can be solved efficiently and the solutions can be used in practical applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power consumption of the ECC checker circuit can be reduced by up to 27%-41% with a negligible impact on area and timing.
the choice of the parity check matrix is a critical design decision for low power ECC.

the choice of the parity check matrix is an important factor in the power optimization problem of ECC checker circuits, and that power can be reduced with little or no increase in area and delay, by considering power along with the traditional area and delay objectives when selecting the parity matrix.
